title: Capacity Rehearsal & Dedicated Sizing — Weekly POC Retro
summary: Third weekly sync for the Helio POC focused on tuning Dedicated sizing and rehearsing a 3x burst scenario for their peak query periods. SE walked through autoscale policy options, warm pool sizing, and a runbook for failover. Customer raised concerns about cold starts, prefix cache TTL and compliance logging. Agreed on a small benchmark run to validate warm pool sizing and an updated cost model for the next call.
next_steps: Priya to run 1-hour surge benchmark with 3x traffic shape and share raw metrics by 2026-11-05
Jordan to send updated dedicated pricing + warm-pool cost model by 2026-11-05
Heliotrope to confirm peak window (timezone + 2-hour stretch) and list of test prompts by 2026-11-04
Schedule follow-up 60-min demo and runbook rehearsal on 2026-11-10
action_items: Priya Nair: Run surge benchmark (3x peak) and upload CSV + graphs; due 2026-11-05
Jordan Lee: Update cost model for Dedicated warm pools and email to procurement; due 2026-11-05
Samir Khan: Provide exact peak window timestamps and sample query mix; due 2026-11-04
Lina Chen: Send SOC2 questions subset to Redwood for matrix mapping; due 2026-11-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Alex Gomez (Redwood Support); Maya Patel (Heliotrope CTO); Ethan Brooks (Platform Eng); Samir Khan (SRE); Lina Chen (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: alright hey everybody, thanks for joining. this is the weekly POC sync, um, capacity rehearsal and sizing retro. we got about 50 minutes so we'll focus on the surge run results and tuning. Priya, you wanna kick us off?

[00:28] Priya: yeah sure, thanks Jordan. quick recap — we ran the staged bursts on Tuesday 11/02, three phases: baseline, 2x and a 3x synthetic traffic profile matching Helio's peak. i have the dashboard open, i'll share screen after this, but top-level: 3x caused increased queueing at the ingress for about 45 seconds before autoscale reacted — we had an aggressive scale policy but cold instance spin-up added 18 to 24s tail latency on first requests.

[01:05] Maya: i, uh, sorry to interrupt — when you say "cold instance" do you mean the GPU VM boot time or model load time? what's the main contributor?

[01:15] Priya: good q — primarily model load + tokenizer init on the first inference container. on Dedicated with warm-pools we can keep x machines pre-warmed; that's the warm pool idea. the boot time of the VM was smaller, like 5 to 8s, model load was dominant, 12 to 16s depending on quantization.

[01:42] Ethan: is that the same for the smaller context, like the 512 token jobs we run? our average is 220 tokens per request but peak sometimes hits 800+ tokens.

[01:55] Priya: token length increases decode time obviously, but load time is model-in-memory; so even short requests see the cold penalty if model isn't resident. for variable seqs we suggest a warm pool sized by steady-state qps plus a buffer — we recommended 20% buffer in the doc but in practice 30% gave smoother tail for 3x.

[02:20] Samir: okay, can you re-state what 3x looked like? we had the spreadsheet but I want the shape — was it spiky or sustained?

[02:30] Priya: it was a 10-minute ramp to 3x sustained for 12 minutes then a drop; shape was realistic — small microbursts within that window. so you saw repeated cold starts as warm pool drained and new instances didn't get primed fast enough.

[03:00] Jordan: quick note on terminology — sorry if i mangle product names, sometimes the transcription says "Redwood Dedicate" — we mean Redwood Dedicated, warm pools, and autoscale policies.

[03:12] Lina: security Q — during the surge did any logs or request traces hit customer-accessible storage outside our VPC? we need to confirm audit log residency.

[03:24] Alex: short answer: no, all telemetry during the POC stayed in the private test VPC you provided. that said, we did forward aggregated metrics to our monitoring plane for dashboarding; we can disable that if you need.

[03:40] Lina: can you list which fields are forwarded? we have to check PII and PHI filters.

[03:47] Alex: it's only high-level counters and latencies — no request body. the traces are sample ids; we don't forward payloads.

[04:00] Priya: back to sizing — we tried two autoscale policies: policy A was reactive (scale when queue > 40 for 30s), policy B had predictive warm-provisioning (based on schedule + recent 5-min throughput). policy A was cheaper at steady-state but failed the 3x burst rehearse due to spin-up. policy B cost more by ~12% but kept 95th latency under SLA.

[04:37] Ethan: roughly what's the warm-pool size we should target? our baseline is 120 rps, typical concurrency 18.

[04:48] Priya: for your numbers, baseline 120 rps with concurrency 18 suggests a steady pool of 8 instances; for 3x burst we recommend warm pool 24 instances to cover sustained peaks, plus autoscale headroom. that's the 3x math.

[05:10] Maya: that seems large, what's the cost impact monthly? we need ballpark to run this past procurement.

[05:18] Jordan: i'll send a model but top-level: keeping warm pools sized for 3x is roughly N * cost_per_instance * hours * 0.7 (we apply utilization factor). Priya will include exact numbers; prelim shows ~18% increase vs aggressive reactive.

[05:37] Samir: alternative — can we do a hybrid: smaller warm pool plus sustained KV cache priming? we pre-warm prefixes so model load is faster?

[05:48] Priya: yes, prefix/KV cache priming helps. if your traffic has many repeated prompts or shared prefixes we can prime the KV cache to reduce model decode time for warm-up. priming cut median tail by ~20% in our internal runs, but it requires predictable prompt surface.

[06:10] Ethan: our prod has high variance in prompts, so priming might have limited effect. we can probably prime the top 30% of templates though.

[06:20] Priya: that will still help. also worth noting: quantization profiles — moving to int8 reduced model load size and cut load times by ~30% in the run, at potential tradeoff in output quality. we logged a few regressions but nothing major for your regulatory templates.

[06:45] Lina: about compliance — audit logs, key management — we need evidence that keys never leave our KMS. do you support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated?

[06:56] Alex: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM supported for Private and Dedicated with network boundaries. for this POC we used a test KMS stub. we'll put together the mapping sheet.

[07:12] Jordan: i'll add that to the matrix. back to the surge: Priya, can you talk about fallback policies? e.g., degrade to a smaller model or reduce max tokens automatically?

[07:24] Priya: sure — we support policy-based fallback. you can route to a lighter quantized variant or enforce token caps per-request under load. e.g., at 90% CPU we switch new requests to the q4_2 variant — cheaper and faster. we instrumented that in the run and saw graceful degradation with reduced latency but slightly different wording in responses.

[07:50] Maya: how do we validate that semantic quality drop is acceptable? we need an eval hook.

[07:58] Priya: we can attach your prompt set and run automatic evals between the primary and fallback model; Redwood Optimize can surface regressions. we'll include a small eval in the benchmark Priya runs.

[08:12] Samir: any post-mortem from the last run? you mentioned a 45s ingress queue earlier — what was the main chokepoint?

[08:22] Priya: ingress queueing came from burst fan-in to a single shard that was at max concurrency; our routing could have been more spread. for the rehearsal we intentionally used your single regional endpoint; in prod we recommend multi-shard and region-aware routing to smooth spikes.

[08:45] Ethan: region-aware routing — we prefer single-region due to data residency. can region-aware be within the same region but across AZs/shards?

[08:55] Priya: yes, same-region multi-AZ shards is typical. that preserves residency but gives routing options.

[09:05] Lina: question on logs again — if we enable more detailed traces for debugging, will that increase telemetry forwarding? we need to know retention and access controls.

[09:16] Alex: more detailed traces are stored in your VPC logs; by default we set a 7-day retention on the demo; we can change retention and role-based access. we also have an audit export you can pull nightly.

[09:34] Jordan: wrapping into next steps — we need the Helio team to provide final peak window and example prompts; Redwood will run a targeted benchmark to validate warm pool sizing and fallback behavior.

[09:46] Maya: quick operational ask — can the benchmark include a sustained 30-minute stretch at 2.5x followed by a 15-minute 3x spike? that's what ops is worried about.

[09:58] Priya: yes we can do that distribution, we'll add a microburst pattern inside the spike. that's a good rehearsal.

[10:08] Samir: operational runbook — can we rehearse failover to a smaller model, measure degradation, and see rollback steps? we need step-by-step to hand to on-call.

[10:20] Jordan: good call — we'll schedule a dedicated runbook rehearsal during the follow-up on 11/10.

[10:28] Ethan: one more perf nuance — do you do continuous KV cache eviction or TTL-based? we saw cache churn in the run.

[10:36] Priya: TTL plus LRU heuristics. you can pin prefixes (pin list) for fixed keys to avoid eviction during peaks. that is a manual step but we'll show how to programmatically pin top-k prefixes.

[10:50] Lina: security again — after the benchmark we need artifacts for our audit: run logs, config snapshot, and a mapping of what was in the warm pool. can you commit to deliver those?

[11:00] Alex: yes we'll deliver the artifacts: run CSVs, config JSON (sanitized), and a warm-pool snapshot. note: we'll sanitize any sampled traces to remove payloads.

[11:12] Jordan: okay let's do a quick recap of owners...

[11:18] Maya: oh also procurement asked about minimum committed capacity for Dedicated — do you have a low-risk pilot contract option?

[11:26] Jordan: we have a short-term reserved pilot for enterprise — 3 month minimum with flexible burst credits. i'll include the term sheet in the pricing email.

[11:36] Priya: final technical note — we saw a ~11% improvement when we switched to int8 quantization for model load; if Helio needs deterministic outputs for regulated templates, we should run a side-by-side eval.

[11:52] Samir: sounds good. i'm comfortable with the proposed plan; we'll provide peak window and prompt list by Wednesday.

[12:00] Jordan: perfect — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the 11/10 rehearsal. ending now.

End of transcript.
